free_tier.stated: Sold in 256 GB chunks at $1.25/mo. Max 10 TB per Slab, max 8 Slabs per KVM Slice = 80 TB theoretical. Requires an accompanying KVM slice in the same facility. Available Las Vegas, New York, Miami, Luxembourg.

egress.terms: 'Unmetered Bandwidth' on every slice, governed by a fair-use rule the company states publicly on LET: 'The rule-of-thumb for WAN (internet-facing connections) is 100Mbit/s of 24/7 usage per every 4GB of memory with a purchased slice. We do, however, allow our customers to burst their usage up to 1Gbit/s during times of lower network use.' A second formulation from a customer cites 'FUP is 25 Mbps per 1GB of RAM for the 95th percentile'. So the storage is metered-free but the sustained rate is tied to how much RAM you bought — on the $3.50/mo 1 GB slice that is ~25 Mbps sustained, i.e. ~8 TB/mo. Internal traffic between services in the same location is genuinely unmetered and unbilled.

interface_detail: block (attach as disk), then sftp/rsync/nfs from the slice
tooling: anything — it is a raw block device on a KVM slice
chaining: Hot-pluggable between slices in the same facility with no reboot, which makes it easy to re-front with a different server. No object API at all ('We may consider an Object Store product down the line, but not at this time').
limits_note: per-object-cap: none. Downgrade impossible — you must order a new slab and migrate. 10 TB hard cap per slab. Requires a base slice, so the true entry cost is a slice plus a slab.
reliability_note: Frantech, operating since 2010, the most consistently recommended block-storage product on LET for a decade. Known friction: signup must come from a residential ISP and is refused from VPN/Tor/datacenter IPs, P.O. boxes rejected — a real obstacle for a privacy-conscious buyer but not an identity-document requirement. Storage is 'enterprise 7200RPM hard drives with an NVME cache and a 40Gbit+ InfiniBand'.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: 'Block Storage Slabs are sold in chunks of 256GB for $1.25/month. A 1TB Block Storage Slab is $5.00/month, with a 10TB Block Storage Slab being just $50.00/month', max 10 TB/slab, max 8 slabs, four locations

'FUP is 25 Mbps per 1GB of RAM for the 95th percentile'
'Registration and ordering must come from a user's residential ISP ... P.O. boxes and mail-forwarding addresses are refused'

price_per_tb_month: $5.00/TB/mo flat, plus the base slice. At 5 TB: $25/mo slab + $3.50 slice = $28.50/mo = $5.70/TB all-in. At 20 TB: 2x 10 TB slabs = $100/mo + $3.50 = $103.50/mo = $5.18/TB. The all-in figure is what matters and it is worse than the headline because the slice is mandatory overhead.
